title: "Stuff goes into the computer and doesn't come out": a cross-tool study of personal information management
venue_or_status: CHI 2004; institutional record and author manuscript
evidence_note: Selected author-manuscript sections reviewed. Thirty-one experienced users; eight in longitudinal phase. Strategies varied across files, email, and bookmarks; browsing preference was reported.
limitation: Mostly university-affiliated convenience sample, dated tools, and self-report; no LLM-agent evaluation.

title: Information behaviour that keeps found things found
venue_or_status: Information Research 10(1), paper 207
evidence_note: Methods and results sections inspected: workplace keeping study, delayed cued re-finding, and survey of 214 people. Keeping methods provided different functions and retrieval routes.
limitation: Previously encountered Web sites and provided task cues; results do not establish open-ended discovery or long-term preservation.

title: The user-subjective approach to personal information management systems design: Evidence and implementations
venue_or_status: Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology 59(2), 235–246; online 2007
evidence_note: Methods, findings, and limitations inspected. Interviews, questionnaires, and screen captures examined project, importance, and context attributes; proposed interfaces explicitly needed further testing.
limitation: Much evidence was self-reported; design proposals and LLM-memory effects were not validated.

title: Folder versus tag preference in personal information management
venue_or_status: Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology 64(10), 1995–2012; accessible publisher abstract
evidence_note: Abstract reports 75 Gmail and 23 Windows 7 participants, folder preference, mostly single-tag use, and lower success/slower retrieval in the tag condition.
limitation: Abstract-only review; complete methods, effect sizes, and statistical analysis not inspected. Results concern the tested interfaces and human users.

title: Faceted Metadata for Image Search and Browsing
venue_or_status: CHI 2003; author-hosted paper
evidence_note: Selected paper sections reviewed. Thirty-two art history students compared faceted and baseline search interfaces for approximately 35,000 images; 90% preferred the faceted approach overall.
limitation: Domain-specific collection, metadata, tasks, and users. Preference does not establish accurate automated metadata or agent task success.

title: It's Not That Important: Demoting Personal Information of Low Subjective Importance Using GrayArea
venue_or_status: CHI 2009; author-institution publication summary
evidence_note: Author-institution summary reports a cleaning task with 96 participants, 13% reduced folder clutter, and 81% finding demotion easier than deletion.
limitation: Summary-level review of a short interface-specific task; does not establish long-term quality or accurate agent context selection.

title: Managing personal information: tactics, strategies and outcomes
venue_or_status: Interacting with Computers, iwaf054; early online 12 December 2025; institutional author record
evidence_note: Institutional abstract reports nine behavior clusters, modest reported retrieval advantages for active management, reuse benefits of filing, and a detrimental association with deletion.
limitation: Abstract-only review; study methods, sample details, effect sizes, and confounding controls not inspected. No causal retention rule inferred.

title: The future of personal information management in the age of ubiquitous personal data
venue_or_status: Human–Computer Interaction 41(1), 1–5; published online 27 March 2025; author-hosted article
evidence_note: AI and theory/methods discussion inspected. The special-issue introduction outlines current research problems and potential tensions in automating personal organization.
limitation: Editorial synthesis rather than a new controlled experiment; references to other papers are not treated as independently reviewed evidence.

title: The PARA Method: The Simple System for Organizing Your Digital Life in Seconds
venue_or_status: Tiago Forte / Forte Labs; published 24 February 2023, updated 15 April 2026
evidence_note: Creator description defines the four categories and organizes information by its role in current commitments.
limitation: Practice and advocacy; no controlled comparison or agent performance evaluation reviewed.

title: Johnny.Decimal: Introduction
year_basis: Consulted version year; page does not state its original publication date
venue_or_status: Undated current creator documentation; consulted October 2026
evidence_note: Current documentation describes area/category/ID organization, stable numeric locations, constrained branching, and an index.
limitation: Publication year unknown; 2026 is the reviewed version year. Benefits are creator claims, not measured agent results.

title: Communicating with Slip Boxes: An Empirical Account
venue_or_status: Niklas Luhmann; Manfred Kuehn English translation of 1981 essay; translation cataloged by Niklas Luhmann Archive
evidence_note: First-person description inspected. Translation date and original essay relation verified against the official archive bibliography record.
limitation: Reflective single-person practice account, despite the subtitle; no controlled comparative evidence or validated LLM cognitive analogy.

title: Why PARA Is the Key to the AI Era
venue_or_status: Tiago Forte / Forte Labs; 13 April 2026
evidence_note: Creator article argues for PARA in AI-assisted work and reports a personal filing experiment; used as current practice testimony only.
limitation: Anecdotal creator experiment and advocacy; no controlled AI memory accuracy or speed result inferred.

title: Announcing Version 2.1 of the NDSA Levels of Digital Preservation
venue_or_status: National Digital Stewardship Alliance; 23 March 2026 release announcement
evidence_note: Official release announcement inspected; confirms sustainability guidance and that Level 4 need not be every organization's goal across all functional areas.
limitation: Preservation-program guidance and release description, not a full conformity audit or experiment on agent semantic accuracy.

title: Reference Model for an Open Archival Information System (OAIS)
venue_or_status: CCSDS 650.0-M-3, Recommended Practice, December 2024
evidence_note: Selected terminology and mandatory-responsibility sections inspected, including independent understandability, representation information, traceability, and documented deletion strategies.
limitation: Archival reference model, not a filesystem recipe; archival understandability and authenticity do not certify claim truth or current applicability.

title: The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)
venue_or_status: RFC 8493, Informational, October 2018
evidence_note: Definitions and payload/validation sections inspected; validity concerns complete packages and verified checksums over opaque payload bytes.
limitation: Packaging and integrity semantics; no guarantee of factual truth, authority, confidentiality, or correct context selection.

title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata, Version 3.0
venue_or_status: PREMIS Editorial Committee / Library of Congress; June 2015, revised November 2015
evidence_note: Selected introduction, data-model, and implementation sections inspected; four core entity types support documenting digital objects and preservation actions.
limitation: Preservation metadata scope; the term Agent is not specific to an LLM, and documenting actions does not verify every assertion's truth.

title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
venue_or_status: W3C Recommendation, 30 April 2013
evidence_note: Selected model definitions inspected; provides relations for tracing production, derivation, revision, and invalidation of entities.
limitation: Provenance representation and validity are distinct from factual validation, domain authority, and present applicability.

title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
venue_or_status: Scientific Data 3, 160018; 15 March 2016
evidence_note: Principles and implementation-scope discussion inspected; includes qualified relations, provenance, permitted authorization, and persistent metadata after unavailable data.
limitation: High-level implementation-independent guidance, not a quality certificate or requirement to release all data publicly.

title: The TRUST Principles for digital repositories
venue_or_status: Scientific Data 7, 144; 14 May 2020
evidence_note: Principle descriptions inspected, including stated preservation timeframes, accountability, user-community needs, and feedback about data fitness.
limitation: Repository stewardship principles, not direct evidence of accurate agent retrieval or generation.

title: DCMI Metadata Terms
venue_or_status: Dublin Core Metadata Initiative Usage Board specification, issued 20 January 2020
evidence_note: Specification header and selected property definitions inspected; established terms distinguish source, modification, versions, replacement, temporal description, and rights.
limitation: Descriptive vocabulary; filling a field does not establish correctness, an effective date, or the authoritative version for a task.

title: HTTP Framework for Time-Based Access to Resource States -- Memento
venue_or_status: RFC 7089, Informational independent submission, December 2013
evidence_note: Abstract, status, and selected protocol sections inspected; datetime negotiation and TimeMaps distinguish prior states and frozen historical representations.
limitation: Not Standards Track; does not guarantee capture completeness, factual accuracy, or that historical content should govern present decisions.
